answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can submit one vote per round. Calling a bot zephyr or oasis does nothing to bypass the deposit: an attacker can forge names freely, but 1,000 voting identities require $100,000 locked up. This ties voting power to scarce capital, and the attacker pays financing costs or forgoes other uses of that money throughout the lockup.
